Subject: Re: Evaluation & SLO targets — FinBank POC

Thanks for the demo today — good conversation. Wrapping up items from our side so we can get to a reproducible run: 

Summary of FinBank goals (from call):
- Primary SLO: interactive latency for customer-facing assistant. Target: p95 end-to-end <= 250 ms for 8k-context queries; p50 ~ 70-90 ms.
- Streaming requirement: partial tokens must appear no more than 50ms after generation; bursty token rates acceptable but tail should be constrained.
- Throughput/concurrency: target sustained concurrency of 200 simultaneous open sessions, peak burst to 500. Typical tokens/sec workload ~ 6k-12k/sec depending on session mix.
- Response length distribution: median reply ~ 40 tokens, 95th ~ 420 tokens (some long form repair flows).

What we need from Redwood before we hand off to your bench team:
1) Clear measurement definitions (warm vs cold start, how p95 computed — per-request, per-token, or wall-clock end-to-end).
2) Exact harness you will run (script, seed prompts, tokenization steps) and whether you will run on hosted or dedicated capacity.
3) Reproducibility checklist (random seeds, model artifact hashes, quantization details).
4) Any security or data-handling requirements to run with our sample prompts (we can sanitize).

Attached: prod_prompt_samples_v1.csv (sample prompt mix). Please confirm a proposed timeframe to run an initial evaluation (2–3 day window preferred).

-Taylor
Lead Platform Engineer, CloudPlatform (FinBank partner)

Hi Taylor / Priya — great to meet you both. Appreciate the clear targets. Below is our proposed measurement and handoff plan so we’re aligned before the bench run. I’ve attached the eval harness and a starter prompt set (redwood_eval_harness_v1.zip).

Quick recap of Redwood definitions we’ll use:
- "End-to-end latency": time from request received by Redwood API to final token emitted (includes our network hop in hosted runs). For Dedicated we can run with local network measurements and will indicate both.
- "Warm run": model KV cache pre-warmed with similar prefixes; we’ll do a 5 minute warmup period at target concurrency. "Cold run": first request after model load (we’ll measure cold-start separately with single-request sampling).
- Percentile calculations: p50/p95/p99 on wall-clock per-request latency, computed on completed requests within the measurement window (exclude warmup window).
- Streaming latency: we’ll measure time-to-first-byte (TTFB) and average inter-token gap; requirement: TTFB <= 50ms and median inter-token gap <= 20ms under nominal load.

Benchmark methodology (high-level):
1) Tokenization: use FinBank's tokenization script (we’ll apply their provided CSV to mirror production token boundaries).
2) Workload shaping: reproduce session mix from prod_prompt_samples_v1.csv (attached), run for 30 minutes steady-state, plus 10 minute ramp up and 10 minute cooldown.
3) Concurrency profiles: run at nominal (200) and stress (500) concurrency levels. We’ll also sweep batch sizes to measure cost/latency tradeoffs.
4) Model variants: evaluate your chosen model plus a quantized int8 variant. We’ll record model hashes and library versions for reproducibility.
5) Metrics emitted: per-request latency (wall-clock), tokens/sec, GPU utilization, memory pressure, and error/fallback rates.

Deliverables we’ll produce:
- Raw logs + parsed CSV of per-request latencies and token-level events.
- A reproducibility README listing exact container image, kernel versions, model artifact checksum, and harness commit hash.
- A short runbook with config used (batch sizes, concurrency, warmup schedule).

Proposed dates: run next week (Oct 19–21) if FinBank can approve prompt set and sign off on the minimal NDA. 

Next steps / asks from FinBank:
- Confirm you’re okay with the definitions above (esp. p95 semantics / warmup window).
- Provide final prompt set (sanitized) or confirmation to use the attached sample.
- Confirm test environment: hosted vs Redwood Dedicated. Dedicated gives us more accurate network-less latency.

I’ll coordinate our bench schedule once we get a thumbs up.

Thanks,
Vanessa Ortiz
Senior Account Exec — Redwood Inference
